deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE. This is a station adjustment (Stationsausgleichung) for Zeven, a station of Gauss's Hanoverian arc measurement. It uses all angle measurements of 1824 and 1825, excluding those of 4 and 5 August. The next page does the same for Bremen.

(1) APPROXIMATE DIRECTIONS. Provisional direction values are listed, with unknown corrections:
- 1 Steinberg: 1°17'45.262" + a
- 2 Brüttendorf 'Strich': 17°21'58.264". This is the fixed reference direction, with no unknown.
- Brüttendorf C: 17°21'48.275". This is an auxiliary point; its '+f' is struck out.
- Bremen C: 53°26'10.871". Auxiliary point.
- 3 Bremen Heliotrop: 53°26'13.375" + b
- 4 Brillit: 124°13'47.128" + c
- 5 Selsingen: 152°47'56.646" + d
- 6 Litberg: 246°0'49.110" + e
- 7 Wilsede: 288°22'42.653" + f

A second column of small numbers (+0.067, +0.579, +0.146, −0.895, +1.219, −0.484, −0.323) is not fully explained. Two of its entries are evidently corrections of the normal-equation constants (see (5)). 'CC +0.027' is probably the constant correction mentioned on the next page; unsure.

(2) OBSERVATION EQUATIONS. For each measured angle i.k, the columns are: label; weight p; the split of p into l/r (circle-left / circle-right repetitions, which sum to p in every row: 35+22=57, 40+28=68, ...); and the observed angle A.

Gauss forms the residual v = (D_k − D_i) − A + (x_k − x_i), with x_k the unknown attached to direction k. For example, 1.3 gives (53°26'13.375 − 1°17'45.262) − 52°8'27.798 = +0.315, so v = +0.315 − a + b.

I recomputed all 13 constants and they are correct: +0.315, +0.263, −0.033, +0.247, −0.776, +0.977, +0.806, −0.035, +0.077, −1.235, +1.201, +1.555, +0.140.
- For 6.1, 6.3, 7.1 and 7.3, 360° is added to the far direction.
- For 7.2 (Wilsede–Brüttendorf), the computed difference is 88°59'15.611" against 15.612" observed. Since direction 2 is fixed, the residual would be about −0.001 − f. Gauss strikes the line through and does not use it.
- The last observation is the combined angle 3.4 + 3.1 (weight 1/2), 18°39'5.500". Its computed value is (c−b)+(a−b) = 18°39'5.640", so v = +0.140 + a − 2b + c.

(3) NORMAL EQUATIONS. Minimising Σ p v² gives Σ p v ∂v/∂x = 0 for each unknown:
- [a]: +1.036 + 214.5a − 58b − 67.5c − 9d − 53e − 27f = 0
- [b]: −0.178 − 58a + 212b − 133c − 16d − 2e − 3f = 0
- [c]: +0.346 (correctly +0.146) − 67.5a − 133b + 264.5c (correctly 260.5) − 12d − 48f = 0
- [d]: −1.189 (correctly −0.989) − 9a − 16b − 12c + 37d = 0
- [e]: −0.036 − 53a − 2b + 100e − 45f = 0
- [f]: +0.021 − 27a − 3b − 48c − 45e + 123f = 0

I verified every coefficient and constant from the weights. All agree except the three items noted in parentheses (see Errors).

(4) ITERATIVE SOLUTION (relaxation). This is Gauss's 'indirect' method, i.e. Gauss–Seidel / Southwell relaxation. Units are 0.001".
- Start from the constants (1036, −178, 346, −1189, −36, 21).
- Repeatedly choose the equation with the largest residual relative to its diagonal and set an integer increment for that unknown. Update all six residuals by adding increment × that column of coefficients.
- The sequence is d=+31, a=−3, b=+2, e=−1, d=+1, f=−1, e=−1, a=−1, f=−1, e=−1.
- Successive residual vectors include, for example, after d=+31: (757, −674, −26, −42, −36, 21); after a=−3: (113.5, −500, 176.5, −15, 123, 102). Every entry checks.
- The final vector is (−13, −22, 62, −1, −38, 12).
- Totals: a = −4, b = +2, c = 0, d = +32, e = −3, f = −2 (×0.001"). The corrections to the provisional directions are therefore negligible: at most 0.032" (Selsingen).

(5) WHICH CONSTANTS THE ITERATION USED. The table works with the erroneous constants 346 and −1189. The first step proves this: c: 346 − 12·31 = −26 and d: −1189 + 37·31 = −42.
- The marginal figures +0.146 (c row) and −0.989 (beside Bremen C / the d row) are the correct values. Gauss apparently noticed the slip afterwards.
- With the corrected constants, the final residuals for c and d would be about −138 and +199. A further step d ≈ −5, plus small adjustments of the other unknowns, would be needed.
errors: Normal-equation constant of the c-row is written +0.346. Recomputed: 68·0.263 + 132·0.247 − 12·0.977 − 48·0.806 + 0.5·0.140 = +0.146. The marginal '+0,146' appears to be Gauss's own correction, but the relaxation table was run with 0.346.
Normal-equation constant of the d-row is written −1.189. Recomputed: −9·0.033 − 16·0.776 + 12·0.977 = −0.989. A marginal '−0,989' seems to be the correction; again the relaxation used −1.189.
Diagonal coefficient of c is written +264.5 (if read correctly). The weights give 68+132+12+48+0.5 = 260.5. This coefficient is never used in the relaxation, so it has no effect there.
Because of the two constant slips, the computed corrections (in particular d = +0.032") are not the exact least-squares solution. The effect is only a few hundredths of an arcsecond.

results.what: Weighted least-squares station adjustment of directions at Zeven from repeated angle measurements. Weights equal numbers of repetitions; one direction is held fixed; a combined angle enters with weight 1/2.
results.modern_name: Station adjustment by least squares (direction/angle adjustment, Stationsausgleichung)

results.what: Iterative solution of the 6×6 normal equations by successively relaxing the largest residual with integer increments in units of 0.001".
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (letter to Gerling 26 Dec 1823; published by Gerling 1843), Seidel 1874, Southwell 1940s (relaxation)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine working sheet of Gauss's geodetic practice. It shows a station adjustment with normal equations solved by his known indirect (Gauss–Seidel-type) method, as described in his 1823 letter to Gerling. It is a nice concrete example, including self-corrected arithmetic slips, but nothing new.

checkable.asserts: Final residuals of relaxation with Gauss's (uncorrected) constants equal (-13,-22,62,-1,-38,12)

transcription_corrections: a-row normal equation: '− 61,50' should read '− 67,5c' (confirmed by the relaxation step a=−3: −26+202.5=176.5).
Margin beside Bremen C: '−0,895 [?]' is '−0,895 −0,989'; −0,989 is the corrected d-row constant.
The '+0,146' on the Strich line is a correction of the c-row constant +0,346.
Last relaxation column header is 'e = −1'; its fifth entry is −38, not −30 (17+45−100... i.e. 62−100).
Label '3.5' is written over '2.5'; the column 'l. r' gives circle-left/right repetition counts summing to the weight.
